# Parasites

> *How do life cycles explain where a parasite is caught, where it lives, and how it is found?*

::: {.callout-note}
## In preparation
This chapter will follow the same template as the *Gram-positive cocci* chapter. The outline below
shows what it will cover.
:::

**The group in one sentence:** Eukaryotic organisms that live on or in a host: single-celled protozoa and many-celled worms (helminths).

**How members differ (the sorting key):** Protozoa versus helminths; life cycle (infective and diagnostic stages); definitive and intermediate hosts.

**Main organisms (full profile cards):** *Plasmodium* (mosquito and human stages), *Giardia* (cysts in water), *Toxoplasma* (cats and other hosts), *Ascaris* (eggs in soil).

**Supporting organisms (one table row each):** *Entamoeba*, *Cryptosporidium*, hookworms, *Strongyloides*, tapeworms, *Schistosoma*.

**Later in the course:** Malaria, gut parasites and others in the organ blocks; antiparasitic drugs in pharmacology.
